name: ADS7042IDCUR
title: 12-bit, 1-MSPS, single-ended SAR ADC with SPI-compatible output, nanowatt-class power
summary: ADS7042 is a 12-bit successive-approximation converter that runs at up to 1 MSPS from a 16-MHz serial clock. Its analog supply AVDD (1.65 V to 3.6 V) is also the reference, so the input span is 0 V to AVDD; a separate DVDD (1.65 V to 3.6 V) powers the three-wire serial port. Power falls in step with sample rate; from a 3 V AVDD it dissipates at most 690 µW running at 1 MSPS and 69 µW at 100 kSPS, and typically 234 µW at 1 MSPS from 1.8 V. An internal offset calibration is started by clocking a long frame. It comes in an 8-pin VSSOP (DCU) and an 8-pin 1.5 mm × 1.5 mm X2QFN (RUG), rated -40 °C to 125 °C.

operation.text: A falling edge on CS freezes the voltage between AINP and AINM and starts a conversion clocked by SCLK. While converting, both inputs are cut off from the sampling capacitors; once the result is done they are reconnected and the part is acquiring again. A 16-MHz SCLK is enough for 1 MSPS, and the result has no pipeline delay.

There is no separate reference pin: AVDD is the reference, and it draws switched-capacitor current. Decouple it with a 1 µF low-ESR ceramic; 200 nF is the smallest value allowed. Feed AVDD from a low-noise, low-output-impedance regulator, such as the TPS79101.

The input is single-ended: the result is AINP minus AINM. AINP takes 0 V to AVDD. AINM accepts -100 mV to +100 mV, so a remote sensor's ground can be brought to AINM on its own wire to take out a small ground difference. Each input passes through a low-pass stage (about 50 Ω and 10 pF) and then a switch of about 50 Ω (Rs) onto a 15 pF sampling capacitor (CS); ESD diodes clamp both inputs to AVDD and GND.

One CS-low period is one frame. Allow tSU_CSCK from CS falling to the first SCLK falling edge. The first zero appears on SDO at CS falling; the second zero and then D11 down to D0 come out on the next SCLK falling edges, so a full result takes 14 clocks. After that SDO stays low until CS rises, which puts SDO in 3-state. Leave at least tACQ after a conversion before the next sample.

An internal offset calibration register, not readable over the interface, corrects every result. It clears to zero at power-up, so a calibration at power-up is advised; it can be repeated later if temperature or AVDD has moved. During calibration both inputs are disconnected from the sampling stage. Only cycling AVDD returns the part to its power-up state and clears the stored offset.

Calibration begins on the opening CS falling edge once power is applied. Hold CS low through 16 or more falling SCLK edges and SDO reads all zeros; with fewer, the register is not updated. Allow the minimum acquisition time before taking the first real sample. SCLK during calibration is limited to 16 MHz above AVDD = 2.25 V and 12 MHz below.

Give a frame 32 or more SCLK falling edges: the first 14 deliver the current result, calibration starts on the 17th edge and finishes on the 32nd, and SDO is low from the 14th edge until CS rises. A frame shorter than 32 clocks leaves the register unchanged.

The front end is an amplifier followed by an RC low-pass: a series RFLT and a CFLT across AINP-AINM. CFLT supplies the charge the sampling capacitor takes and absorbs kickback; make it at least 20 × 15 pF (over 300 pF) and C0G/NP0. RFLT isolates the amplifier from that capacitance; larger values help stability but add distortion with source impedance, frequency and amplitude, so it is a trade-off. Check by SPICE that the amplifier keeps more than 40° phase margin, and that it settles to the needed accuracy within the acquisition window.

operation.topic: Running from a sensor without a driver
operation.text: For slow signals where lowest power matters more than ENOB, a sensor can drive AINP through its own output resistance into CFLT. A high source resistance needs more acquisition time. At a given throughput, keep SCLK at 16 MHz and lengthen the CS-high time rather than slowing SCLK: at 100 kSPS this gives 9.21875 µs of acquisition against 2.1875 µs at 1.6 MHz.

AVDD runs the converter and DVDD the interface; each can be anywhere in 1.65 V to 3.6 V regardless of the other. Set AVDD at or above the largest input to avoid clipped codes. Decouple each with its own 1 µF ceramic; the minimums are 200 nF on AVDD and 20 nF on DVDD, or 220 nF if one source feeds both.

Run AVDD as close to the largest input as possible (but not below it), run DVDD as low as allowed, keep the SDO load capacitance small, and run no faster than needed: power falls with throughput. DVDD current depends on DVDD, SDO load and the output code.

Put a ground plane under the part and split the board into analog and digital areas; keep digital traces from crossing the analog path and keep analog inputs and AVDD away from noise. In the layout example, analog input and reference run on the top and left sides of the part and digital on the bottom and right. Place the 1 µF AVDD and DVDD capacitors next to their pins with no vias between pin and capacitor; join the AVDD capacitor (CREF) to the AVDD and GND pins with wide copper. Ground pins go to the plane by short, low-impedance paths. Keep the RC input filter close to the part, using C0G (NP0) capacitors.
With DVDD from 1.65 V to 1.95 V the I/O meets JESD8-7A: inputs high above 0.65 DVDD and low below 0.35 DVDD; SDO at 2 mA is within 0.45 V of DVDD high and below 0.45 V low.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A unity-gain op-amp buffer drives AINP through R; C across AINP and AINM forms the RC filter and holds the charge for sampling. AINM and GND go to ground, and AVDD, which doubles as the reference, comes from the AVDD rail. R and C carry no values.
notes: The source VIN+ is referred to ground.

circuits.title: Single-supply DAQ with OPA314
circuits.description: An OPA314 buffer on the AVDD rail drives AINP through 200 Ω into 1.5 nF to ground; AINM is grounded. The target is SNR above 68 dB and THD below -80 dB at 2.5 kHz and 1 MSPS. The OPA314 is chosen for rail-to-rail input and output, 14 nV/√Hz noise and 150 µA supply current.
notes: Measured with a 2.5 kHz input: SNR 69 dB, THD -80 dB, SINAD 68.6 dB (32768 samples).

circuits.title: DAQ for maximum SINAD with OPA835
circuits.description: An OPA835 buffer on its own supplies drives AINP through 25 Ω into 1.5 nF to ground, AINM grounded, aiming for SINAD above 69.5 dB up to 250 kHz. The OPA835 is chosen for 56 MHz bandwidth and 9.3 nV/√Hz noise, enough to settle within the acquisition time and stay under a fifth of the converter's noise.
notes: Measured: 2 kHz input SNR 70.62 dB, THD -83.96 dB, SINAD 70.3 dB; 250 kHz input SNR 70.22 dB, THD -81.58 dB, SINAD 69.8 dB (32768 samples each).

circuits.title: Anti-aliasing filter at the input
circuits.description: The RC network that sits between any driver and the converter: RFLT in series into AINP and CFLT from AINP to AINM, with AINM grounded. Its corner is 1 / (2π × RFLT × CFLT).

circuits.title: Sensor wired straight to the input
circuits.description: A sensor, modelled as a source with output resistance ROUT, feeds AINP directly; CFLT from AINP to AINM is the only added part, and the sensor's return joins AINM and ground. Used for slow signals at low throughput: the 10-kSPS example reached 11.4 ENOB at 7 µW.
notes: With 1.5 nF of CFLT, ENOB holds near 11.3 up to 1 MSPS for 25 Ω and 250 Ω sources and falls with sampling rate for 2.5 kΩ, 10 kΩ and 25 kΩ sources.

circuits.title: Supply decoupling
circuits.description: Each supply pin gets its own 1 µF ceramic to GND: one on AVDD, which also serves as the reference, and one on DVDD.
